content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To enjoy the outdoors, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a high-quality topographical map (20 minutes)
Step 2. Pack a waterproof rain jacket (5 minutes)
Step 3. Snap a panoramic photo of the summit (1 minute)
Step 4. Research local national parks (1 hour)
Step 5. Select a specific hiking trail (15 minutes)
Step 6. Check the mountain weather forecast (10 minutes)
Step 7. Set up the basecamp tent (30 minutes)
Step 8. Apply heavy-duty sunscreen (5 minutes)
Step 9. Charge the portable power bank (4 hours)
Step 10. Withdraw cash for park entrance fees (10 minutes)
Step 11. Pack a lightweight camping stove (10 minutes)
Step 12. Fill the hydration bladder with water (5 minutes)
Step 13. Buy trail mix and protein bars (30 minutes)
Step 14. Clean the hiking boots (15 minutes)
Step 15. Highlight the planned route on the map (10 minutes)
Step 16. Test the stove ignition (5 minutes)
Step 17. Reserve a backcountry campsite (20 minutes)
Step 18. Organize the emergency first aid kit (45 minutes)
Step 19. Inspect the trekking poles (5 minutes)
Step 20. Place the water bladder in the backpack (2 minutes)
Step 21. Renew the annual park pass (15 minutes)
Step 22. Decide on a weekend for the trip (2 days)
Step 23. Download an offline GPS app (10 minutes)
Step 24. Verify the backpack weight (10 minutes)
Step 25. Calibrate the digital compass (5 minutes)
Step 26. Laminate the emergency contact list (15 minutes)
Step 27. Check the car's tire pressure (10 minutes)
Step 28. Purchase sterile bandages and antiseptic (30 minutes)
Step 29. Buy a small canister of fuel (20 minutes)
Step 30. Waterproof the leather boots (2 hours)
Step 31. Pack a pair of polarized sunglasses (2 minutes)
Step 32. Buy a durable 60-liter backpack (1 hour)
Step 33. Pack a set of titanium cookware (5 minutes)
Step 34. Update the phone's operating system (40 minutes)
Step 35. Tighten the trekking pole baskets (5 minutes)
Step 36. Buy lightweight carbon fiber poles (45 minutes)
Step 37. Begin the uphill hike (4 hours)
Step 38. Read online trail reviews (30 minutes)
Step 39. Invite a group of friends (15 minutes)
Step 40. Drive to the park trailhead (3 hours)
